result:
**I'd make radical curiosity and evidence-based truth-seeking the default human operating system.**

Not "more education" in the current sense. Not niceness. Not forced consensus. I'd rewire the baseline so that the overwhelming majority of people felt genuine, visceral pull toward updating their models of reality when better evidence appears, and felt almost allergic to clinging to comforting falsehoods, tribal signals, or authority for its own sake.

### Why this one change
Most of the world's persistent nightmares—poverty traps, preventable disease, pointless wars, stagnant science in some domains, bad policy that ignores incentives, mass delusions that survive contact with data—stem from the same root: minds that optimize for belonging, status, narrative coherence, or short-term emotional relief instead of map accuracy. Curiosity that actually updates is the highest-leverage trait because it compounds. Better maps produce better technology, better coordination, better institutions, and fewer self-inflicted catastrophes. Everything else (energy abundance, multiplanetary life, curing aging, aligned superintelligence, ending scarcity) becomes far more achievable once the agents steering those projects reliably prefer reality over preferred stories.

### What it wouldn't be
- Not making everyone "smart" by IQ points alone. Plenty of high-g people are brilliant at rationalizing nonsense.
- Not enforced orthodoxy or "trust the experts" as a slogan. Experts are often wrong; the method is what matters.
- Not erasing emotion, aesthetics, or values. Those stay. The change is that when facts collide with sacred cows, the cows lose more often.

Humanity already has pockets of this mindset (parts of science, engineering, some markets, certain subcultures). Scaling the disposition itself—making the itch to understand stronger than the itch to belong or dominate—would cascade harder and cleaner than any single invention or policy. The universe is stranger and more interesting than our current stories; I'd rather we actually go look.

That's the lever. Everything else is downstream.
